title: Flooding normalization profile identity and its enumerable universe
description:
Standard LDPC codes in `gf2-coding` carry a canonical flooding-profile identity, and one library function enumerates the finite universe of profiles and default iteration caps that table generation, validation and default lookup share.

## Background

gf2's flooding LDPC decoders use normalized min-sum (NMS) with a family-wide factor of 0.75 for NR (5G) and plain min-sum for generic codes. An indication on DVB-T2 normal rate 1/2 at an iteration cap of 50 shows 0.75 losing more than 0.3 dB to 0.875, with AFF3CT 4.7.0 reproducing both figures, and a sample-based density-evolution (DE) estimate puts the threshold-optimal factor near 0.90 for that code, at least 0.95 for DVB-T2 short rate 1/2, 0.6 to 0.7 for NR at low and middle rates and 0.75 to 0.80 for NR at rates 0.77 to 0.88. The owner decision of @/issue/3461a52a makes the default a table of the DE-optimal factor per code profile and iteration cap, produced by an in-tree offline tool, caller-overridable, and standing only if benchmark-window curves confirm it. A profile with no table entry keeps its current behaviour: generic `LdpcDecoder::new` uses plain min-sum, and NR rate-matched constructors and explicitly selected NMS defaults keep 0.75.

Table generation, window validation and the constructor defaults must agree on which profiles exist, or a table entry can be generated that no constructor resolves, or a constructor can resolve a profile the table never covered. `@/inv/semantic-types` asks for one canonical identity, and `@/inv/single-source-prose` asks that the universe be derived from the code tables rather than copied into a second inventory.

A flooding profile is the semantic identity `FloodingProfile` in `gf2-coding`: a DVB-T2 profile is a (frame size, code rate) pair that `LdpcCode::dvb_t2_short` or `LdpcCode::dvb_t2_normal` in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/core.rs` builds from the tables in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/dvb_t2/dvb_t2_matrices.rs`; an NR profile is a base graph with either the full mother code or a rate-matched transmission pattern of filler and kept-parity base columns derived from `NrRateMatchParams` in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/mod.rs`. Lifting size does not enter the profile, since protograph DE is asymptotic in it. The NR rate-matched universe is every pattern `QuasiCyclicLdpc::nr_5g_rate_matched` reaches over the base-graph dimensions in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/bg1.rs` and `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/bg2.rs`, `kb_for_z_selection` and the lifting sets in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/lifting.rs`. The iteration-cap universe is the library's flooding default caps: `SOFT_DECODE_MAX_ITERATIONS` in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/mod.rs` and the DVB-T2 concatenated decoder's default LDPC cap, which `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/dvb_t2/concat.rs` holds as an unnamed literal today.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `FloodingProfile` identifies DVB-T2 (frame size, rate) profiles and NR mother and rate-matched profiles; the standard DVB-T2 and NR constructors attach their profile to the `LdpcCode` they build, and a code built from a raw parity-check matrix carries none.
- [hard] REQ-02: A rate-matched NR code maps to the profile of its filler and kept-parity base-column pattern, and two codes with the same base graph and pattern at different lifting sizes map to the same profile.
- [hard] REQ-03: One function enumerates the profile universe from the code tables, the base-graph dimensions, `kb_for_z_selection` and the lifting sets; a test checks that every profile a standard constructor attaches over the lifting sets and accepted rates is in the enumeration, and the enumeration contains no profile a constructor cannot produce.
- [hard] REQ-04: The DVB-T2 concatenated decoder's default LDPC cap is a named public constant, and one function returns the default-cap universe from that constant and `SOFT_DECODE_MAX_ITERATIONS`.

## Notes

Decoding behaviour is unchanged: no factor is read from a profile here.

planning.outcome: Standard LDPC codes carry a canonical flooding profile drawn from one enumerated universe

terminal.consumer_family: standard LDPC code constructors in gf2-coding
terminal.test_boundary: gf2-coding unit tests of profile attachment
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One identity type plus its enumeration and constructor attachment is one module-sized change.

title: Density evolution of flooding normalized min-sum on degree distributions
description:
`gf2-coding` computes sample-based density evolution of flooding normalized min-sum on an edge-perspective degree distribution, and finds the threshold-optimal factor at a given iteration cap, so a DVB-T2 profile's factor derives from its degree structure.

## Background

gf2's flooding LDPC decoders use normalized min-sum (NMS) with a family-wide factor of 0.75 for NR (5G) and plain min-sum for generic codes. An indication on DVB-T2 normal rate 1/2 at an iteration cap of 50 shows 0.75 losing more than 0.3 dB to 0.875, with AFF3CT 4.7.0 reproducing both figures, and a sample-based density-evolution (DE) estimate puts the threshold-optimal factor near 0.90 for that code, at least 0.95 for DVB-T2 short rate 1/2, 0.6 to 0.7 for NR at low and middle rates and 0.75 to 0.80 for NR at rates 0.77 to 0.88. The owner decision of @/issue/3461a52a makes the default a table of the DE-optimal factor per code profile and iteration cap, produced by an in-tree offline tool, caller-overridable, and standing only if benchmark-window curves confirm it. A profile with no table entry keeps its current behaviour: generic `LdpcDecoder::new` uses plain min-sum, and NR rate-matched constructors and explicitly selected NMS defaults keep 0.75.

Zhang, Fossorier, Gu and Zhang (GLOBECOM 2005, doi:10.1109/glocom.2005.1577841) choose the factor that minimizes the DE threshold; Emran and Elsabrouty (arXiv:1501.07336) apply it to DVB codes; Chen and Fossorier (IEEE Commun. Lett. 2002, doi:10.1109/4234.1001666) originate the method. DVB-T2 needs only its edge-perspective degree distribution, read from the code tables in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/dvb_t2/`. Under `@/inv/library-first-generality` the DE mathematics is a library API; search orchestration and generation stay in a tool.

Every DE computation declares its seed, sample count, factor grid, threshold precision, stopping rule and iteration cap. The fixed configuration uses seed 3461, a factor grid no coarser than 0.025 over $[0.5, 1.0]$, threshold bisection that stops at 0.05 dB for DVB-T2 and 0.1 dB for NR, over BPSK AWGN with the all-zero codeword. 

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: For a declared configuration, the API returns the DE threshold of a degree distribution at a factor and cap, and the threshold-optimal factor over the factor grid; identical inputs produce identical output.
- [hard] REQ-02: The edge-perspective degree distribution of a DVB-T2 profile derives from its code table, and its node and edge counts match the built `LdpcCode`.
- [hard] REQ-03: The DE reproduces at least one published threshold within declared precision under its published configuration; the Zhang et al. figure of 0.75 and 0.90 dB for the (16200, 7200) code, against the estimate of at least 0.95 and 2.72 dB at 0.75 and the 0.9375 of Emran et al., is recomputed and the outcome is recorded in @/issue/3461a52a with source and configuration.
- [hard] REQ-04: Fast-tier tests use small sample counts within the per-test budget; the published-threshold reproduction runs as a descriptive slow-tier test.

planning.outcome: Flooding NMS density evolution on degree distributions is a deterministic gf2-coding API

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One numerical module with its degree extraction and threshold search fits one focused cycle.

warning_overrides.chain-link: Edge-perspective and protograph DE are separate numerical methods with separate conformance evidence; splitting them keeps each to one focused cycle.

title: Protograph density evolution with punctured and shortened columns
description:
`gf2-coding` computes protograph density evolution of flooding normalized min-sum with punctured and shortened base columns, so an NR mother or rate-matched profile's factor derives from its base graph and transmission pattern.

## Background

gf2's flooding LDPC decoders use normalized min-sum (NMS) with a family-wide factor of 0.75 for NR (5G) and plain min-sum for generic codes. An indication on DVB-T2 normal rate 1/2 at an iteration cap of 50 shows 0.75 losing more than 0.3 dB to 0.875, with AFF3CT 4.7.0 reproducing both figures, and a sample-based density-evolution (DE) estimate puts the threshold-optimal factor near 0.90 for that code, at least 0.95 for DVB-T2 short rate 1/2, 0.6 to 0.7 for NR at low and middle rates and 0.75 to 0.80 for NR at rates 0.77 to 0.88. The owner decision of @/issue/3461a52a makes the default a table of the DE-optimal factor per code profile and iteration cap, produced by an in-tree offline tool, caller-overridable, and standing only if benchmark-window curves confirm it. A profile with no table entry keeps its current behaviour: generic `LdpcDecoder::new` uses plain min-sum, and NR rate-matched constructors and explicitly selected NMS defaults keep 0.75.

NR rate matching in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/mod.rs` punctures the first two systematic base columns, removes parity from the end and shortens filler bits; an edge-perspective distribution loses that structure, so NR needs protograph DE on the base graphs in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/bg1.rs` and `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/bg2.rs`. The optimum depends on rate and iteration cap.

Every DE computation declares its seed, sample count, factor grid, threshold precision, stopping rule and iteration cap. The fixed configuration uses seed 3461, a factor grid no coarser than 0.025 over $[0.5, 1.0]$, threshold bisection that stops at 0.05 dB for DVB-T2 and 0.1 dB for NR, over BPSK AWGN with the all-zero codeword. 

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: For an NR profile and cap, the API returns the protograph DE threshold at a factor and the threshold-optimal factor over the factor grid, with punctured columns entering at zero channel information and filler columns as known bits; identical inputs produce identical output.
- [hard] REQ-02: A regular protograph whose lifted ensemble equals an unstructured degree distribution gives the same threshold as the edge-perspective DE within declared precision.
- [hard] REQ-03: Fast-tier tests stay within the per-test budget; full base-graph runs are slow-tier tests with a descriptive ignore.

planning.outcome: Flooding NMS protograph density evolution covers NR mother and rate-matched profiles

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One protograph extension of an existing DE module is a single focused change.

title: Offline density-evolution tool and the committed flooding factor table
description:
An offline executable `ldpc-density-evolution` computes the DE-optimal flooding factor for one profile and cap and regenerates the committed `FLOODING_NMS_FACTORS` table in `gf2-coding` over the library's enumerated (profile, cap) universe, so the table is reproducible from one command and one fixed configuration.

The tool is a workspace member under `dev/tools/`, like `dev/tools/tuning-campaign-support`. It depends on `gf2-coding` for the profile universe and the DE APIs and holds only CLI, search orchestration and source generation, under `@/inv/library-first-generality` and `@/inv/crate-dependency-direction`; no production crate depends on it. ## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A `compute` command prints the threshold-optimal factor and its threshold for one named profile and cap under the fixed configuration.
- [hard] REQ-02: A `regenerate` command writes the table source for each (profile, cap) pair the library enumerates, takes the universe from the library rather than a list of its own, and records the configuration in the generated file's header; two runs with the same configuration write byte-identical output, checked on a reduced universe in a fast-tier test.
- [hard] REQ-03: The committed table has exactly one entry per enumerated (profile, cap) pair, checked by a fast-tier test against the enumeration, and no decoder default reads it.

title: Window-curve harness for the flooding normalization table
description:
An experiment harness measures FER curves for sampled flooding profiles at the pre-registered candidate factors and applies the pre-registered decision rule, so the window campaigns confirm or falsify table entries mechanically.

## Background

gf2's flooding LDPC decoders use normalized min-sum (NMS) with a family-wide factor of 0.75 for NR (5G) and plain min-sum for generic codes. An indication on DVB-T2 normal rate 1/2 at an iteration cap of 50 shows 0.75 losing more than 0.3 dB to 0.875, with AFF3CT 4.7.0 reproducing both figures, and a sample-based density-evolution (DE) estimate puts the threshold-optimal factor near 0.90 for that code, at least 0.95 for DVB-T2 short rate 1/2, 0.6 to 0.7 for NR at low and middle rates and 0.75 to 0.80 for NR at rates 0.77 to 0.88. The owner decision of @/issue/3461a52a makes the default a table of the DE-optimal factor per code profile and iteration cap, produced by an in-tree offline tool, caller-overridable, and standing only if benchmark-window curves confirm it. A profile with no table entry keeps its current behaviour: generic `LdpcDecoder::new` uses plain min-sum, and NR rate-matched constructors and explicitly selected NMS defaults keep 0.75.

The pre-registered decision rule is fixed before any measurement. Sample: every DVB-T2 (frame size, rate) profile, and per NR base graph the mother code plus the rate-matched profiles at the lowest, median and highest rate of the enumerated universe, each at its library default cap. Candidates per entry: the table factor $\alpha^*$, $\alpha^* \pm 0.05$, 0.75, plain min-sum where it is the current default and, for DVB-T2, the layered configuration's 0.875. Each FER point runs until 100 frame errors or 200 000 frames over BPSK AWGN with seed 3461, random codewords and syndrome stopping; the FER $10^{-3}$ crossing is log-linear interpolation between the bracketing points of a 0.05 dB grid, with an interval from 95% Wilson bounds on those points. An entry is confirmed when the crossing of $\alpha^*$ lies within 0.05 dB of the best candidate's crossing; falsified when a candidate's crossing is better by more than 0.05 dB with non-overlapping intervals; otherwise unconfirmed. The rule stands for a family when every sampled entry is confirmed. A falsified entry is recorded, regenerated with its DE configuration corrected and measured once more; a second falsification rejects the rule for that family. 

The harness lives under `experiments/` and consumes `gf2-coding` and `experiments/common` for run identity and durable publication, under `@/inv/convention-convergence`. It is a campaign under `@/inv/campaign-evidence`: resumable bounded runs, one append-only execution log outside the tracked tree, and a record pinning executable digest, configuration, seed and observed host facts.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The committed configuration states the sample, candidates, stopping rule, seed, grid, crossing estimator, interval and tolerance of the rule above, and the harness takes the sample from the library's profile enumeration.
- [hard] REQ-02: For each sampled entry the harness reports per-candidate crossings with intervals and the entry verdict (confirmed, falsified or unconfirmed); a fast-tier test checks the verdict logic on synthetic curves at the tolerance boundary.
- [hard] REQ-03: A run resumes from its execution log without repeating completed points, and identical seed and configuration give identical counts across worker counts.
- [hard] REQ-04: Each run names harness, configuration, iteration cap and host, and labels runs outside the benchmark window as indications.

planning.outcome: A resumable harness applies the pre-registered rule to sampled flooding profiles

terminal.test_boundary: harness unit tests on synthetic curves
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One experiment crate reusing the shared run mechanics fits one focused cycle.

title: Shared flooding normalization policy over the factor table
description:
One caller-overridable `gf2-coding` policy resolves the flooding normalization of a decode from the code's flooding profile and the actual iteration cap through `FLOODING_NMS_FACTORS`, so constructors, wrappers and routes share one lookup.

## Background

gf2's flooding LDPC decoders use normalized min-sum (NMS) with a family-wide factor of 0.75 for NR (5G) and plain min-sum for generic codes. An indication on DVB-T2 normal rate 1/2 at an iteration cap of 50 shows 0.75 losing more than 0.3 dB to 0.875, with AFF3CT 4.7.0 reproducing both figures, and a sample-based density-evolution (DE) estimate puts the threshold-optimal factor near 0.90 for that code, at least 0.95 for DVB-T2 short rate 1/2, 0.6 to 0.7 for NR at low and middle rates and 0.75 to 0.80 for NR at rates 0.77 to 0.88. The owner decision of @/issue/3461a52a makes the default a table of the DE-optimal factor per code profile and iteration cap, produced by an in-tree offline tool, caller-overridable, and standing only if benchmark-window curves confirm it. A profile with no table entry keeps its current behaviour: generic `LdpcDecoder::new` uses plain min-sum, and NR rate-matched constructors and explicitly selected NMS defaults keep 0.75.

The cap is known only when decoding starts (`decode_iterative(llrs, max_iterations)` in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/core.rs`), so the policy resolves at that point from the profile the code carries. An explicitly selected algorithm or factor always wins. A (profile, cap) pair with no entry resolves to the current behaviour of the decision. This change adds the policy and its contracts; no constructor default switches to it here.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Failing behavioural tests precede the implementation and cover table selection, the actual cap, explicit overrides, absent entries and NR puncture and filler handling.
- [hard] REQ-02: A policy-selected decode produces the same decisions and iteration counts as the same decode with the factor passed explicitly, across the scalar, SIMD, batch and GPU flooding backends' shared conformance suite.
- [hard] REQ-03: The policy's rustdoc states the precedence and the absent-entry behaviour and cites the table as the single source of factors.

planning.outcome: One caller-overridable policy resolves the flooding factor from profile and actual cap

terminal.worker_sized_reason: A lookup policy with its conformance tests in one module is one cycle.

The NR default is the private `DEFAULT_NMS_SCALE` in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/mod.rs`, also documented in `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/batch.rs` and selected by `resolve_algorithm` in `crates/gf2-coding/src/bin/sim_runner.rs`.
